source.title: Advancing diagnostic performance and clinical usability of neural networks via adversarial training and dual batch normalization
source.authors: T. Han; S. Nebelung; F. Pedersoli; Markus Zimmermann; M. Schulze-Hagen; Michael Ho; Christoph Haarburger; F. Kiessling; C. Kuhl; V. Schulz; D. Truhn

record.file_problem: Full paper text and supplementary materials are present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper trains medical image classifiers and studies adversarial robustness, batch normalization, diagnostic performance, saliency ratings, and representations. It does not test whether gradient training reaches near-zero training classification error or the conditions in V1–V6.
record.gate_note: No reported result measures training classification error or tests the initialization, depth, width, learning-rate stability, or batch-normalization claims as stated in the versions. The reported ROC-AUC and saliency-rating outcomes are not training-error results.
record.test_reason: The study uses residual networks and batch normalization, explicitly invoking normalization's optimization rationale, but evaluates diagnostic performance, adversarial robustness, saliency maps and representations. It reports no results testing V1–V6. In particular, dual versus single batch normalization is not a comparison of training speed or learning-rate tolerance with versus without normalization.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors' conclusion: adversarial training with dual batch normalization achieves comparable diagnostic performance to standard training while improving adversarial robustness and the clinical usefulness of saliency maps. The reported nonsignificant diagnostic differences do not establish formal statistical equivalence.
record.recipe_differences: Medical-image adversarial training with standard or dual batch normalization; the study does not implement the training-error recipes in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Diagnostic performance and saliency-map ratings vary with adversarial-training setup (single versus dual batch normalization) and dataset modality/data availability; reported results do not measure the versions' outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: Dual batch normalization during adversarial training improves diagnostic test performance over single batch normalization and yields performance comparable to standard training; saliency maps also receive higher clinical ratings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Separate normalization for real and adversarial inputs can improve diagnostic performance and saliency-map usefulness in medical-image adversarial training.

fits_no_version.finding: In shallow ReLU networks on MNIST and Luna16, stronger adversarial attacks shift learned adversarial-batch normalization scales toward zero (Fig. S1). This measures learned parameters, not training speed or learning-rate tolerance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adversarial perturbation strength affects the normalization scales learned for adversarial inputs.

record.problems: The claim-relevant training error is not reported. AUC comparisons use small internal test sets for some datasets (CheXpert validation: 202 scans); the external test set has 22,433 radiographs. The paper reports confidence intervals and significance tests for diagnostic metrics, but these do not address the versions' training-error outcomes.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-relevant result rows were reported.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error on CIFAR-10/100, including corrupted labels, and its dependence on model size, early stopping or regularization.
Spurious minima and the effect of extra student width in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Training-error degradation with depth and its prevention by identity shortcuts or special initialization.
Initialization-dependent training speed, signal and gradient propagation, and trainable depth.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, transient loss growth, curvature dynamics, recovery and divergence.
Training speed and learning-rate tolerance with versus without batch normalization, including Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: The record's relation 'tests' is incorrect. Its empty result rows and absence of version verdicts are appropriate. Supplementary normalization-scale results and representation-similarity analyses do not supply a test of V6.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, zero or near-zero error, random or corrupted labels, and the effects of model size, early stopping, and regularization are not tested.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student problem, spurious minima, gradient-descent endpoint, or width sweep is reported.
No plain-versus-residual depth comparison or training-error result is reported; the ResNet-50 architecture is used without a depth sweep.
No initialization comparison or signal/gradient propagation measurement is reported.
No learning-rate stability threshold, loss-curvature trajectory, or divergence result is reported.
The paper uses dual batch normalization in adversarial training and reports diagnostic performance, but does not compare training speed or learning-rate tolerance as named by this version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
